description: Maine weatherization provides approved home efficiency improvements at no cost to eligible households. Local community action agencies arrange the assessment and work.
introduction: Maine weatherization provides approved home efficiency improvements at no cost to eligible households. Local community action agencies arrange the assessment and work.

who: Eligible homeowners, renters and certain two-to-four-unit residential properties can qualify. Renters need the owner’s approval.
HEAP participation can establish a pathway, but some households qualify under weatherization rules alone. The agency assesses income and property eligibility.
sections.get: A home assessment identifies appropriate measures, such as insulation, air sealing, ventilation and heating-efficiency work. The work varies by the home’s needs and funding.
sections.docs: Ask the local agency for its current checklist. Prepare income or HEAP eligibility records, utility information and ownership or landlord-contact details. Explain any structural, moisture or safety problem before an assessor visits.
sections.apply:
1. Use the agency directory linked from MaineHousing’s weatherization page.
  2. Contact the local community action agency for an application and waiting-list information.
  3. Arrange the assessment and obtain owner consent if needed.
sections.after: Ask for the approved scope and final-inspection information. Some hazards must be corrected before work can start; request the reason for a deferral and ask about another repair program. Do not order work independently expecting reimbursement.
sections.sources:
• Maine weatherization household guidance
  • USA Assistance background and screenshots

faqs: Do all homes get the same improvements?
No. The assessment determines suitable measures for the particular dwelling.
Not always. MaineHousing says some households qualify under weatherization income rules alone.
Can a landlord with a small apartment building ask about help?
Yes. Eligible two-to-four-unit residential buildings are included, subject to the program’s property requirements.
Can unsafe conditions delay the work?
Yes. Structural, electrical, heating or moisture problems can require correction first. Ask the agency what is needed.

provenance.review_scope: Program purpose, eligibility pathway and application methods; no unverified dollar limits published.
